subject: VPC patch window — risk heatmap & ops check-in
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepayments.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC patch window — risk heatmap & ops check-in

Hi Jordan / Acme Ops team,

We're planning the July maintenance for your Private (VPC) deployment and I wanted to align on the safety plan and runbook before we lock the window. Attached is a first-pass "risk heatmap" (risk-heatmap-v1.xlsx) and a short diff of the ops runbook that highlights new pin/rollback steps (ops-runbook-diff.txt).

High-level plan: 
- Proposed window: Sat 2028-08-03 02:00-06:00 UTC (US-west quiet hours)
- Target change: runtime+networking patch + minor model runtime bump (pinned service_image: rwd-infer:2.7.1 -> 2.8.0)
- Canary & soak: 3 nodes in staging -> 1 prod canary node -> 30m soak -> broad roll (traffic ramp via weighted routing)
- Rollback triggers: elevated 95th p99 latency > 250ms for >5m; error rate >0.8% for 10m; failing KV-resume on pinned sessions; telemetry regression on eval prompt set (>3% RER)

Requests from your side: 
1) Confirm the window or propose alternate 2-hour block on 8/3–8/4
2) Provide a named on-call for the window (ops@ email or primary+backups)
3) Any open compliance audit items that would prevent a staged canary during the window?

Neha, Rishi, Karthik — please review the heatmap and pick any additional checks you'd like the customer to sign off on. I flagged network egress ACL changes and the KV cache migration as medium risk.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC patch window — risk heatmap & ops check-in

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the pre-read and the heatmap. A few quick items from Acme: 

- Window: 8/3 02:00-04:00 UTC is tight for us (we have a small batch job at 03:30 UTC). Can we slide to 03:30-07:30 UTC so the canary happens before the batch starts? If you need a narrower window we can ask the batch team to move, but prefer avoiding it.
- On-call: I'll assign Samir Khatri (samir.khatri@acmepayments.com) as primary and include ops@acmepayments.com as backup.
- Compliance: We have no audit holds but our security team wants confirmation that the KV cache pin will not involve key rotation. Also they asked for a signed list of rollback triggers and a post-mortem template in case we hit a severity-2 incident.

Canary requirement: we require a pre-canned load spike (10% of peak) during the 30m soak to validate autoscaling behavior. Can you confirm Redwood will run the spike and capture traces?

Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Payments
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepayments.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC patch window — risk heatmap & ops check-in

Marissa / Jordan — thanks, reviewed the heatmap. A few operational notes and clarifications (short bullets):

- KV cache pinning: this is a logical pin (cache TTL/namespace change) not a key rotation. We will not re-encrypt keys during the patch. I'll add a callout in the runbook to explicitly state no KMS key rotation during this window.
- Pre-warm & live traffic routing: We'll run prefix pre-warm (60m) targeting the typical conversational prompt set for Acme. Pre-warm will be started 90m before the canary to ensure KV resident warm-up.
- Canary spike: Redwood will execute the 10% synthetic traffic spike and provide an HTTP-level tracebundle + opentelemetry spans. We'll capture: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), token generation errors, and autoscaler scale events. Please provide a sample request profile to mirror production traffic (size/seq length).
- Rollback choreography (ops-runbook-diff.txt highlights):
  * Step 1: Pause ingress routing to new pods; advance traffic back to pinned revision
  * Step 2: Evacuate KV-backed sessions from canary pods to stable pool (script: evict_kv_canary.sh)
  * Step 3: Re-deploy previous runtime image and clear ephemeral caches
  * Step 4: Verify p50/p95 within baseline and run the smoke eval set
  * Abort if any trigger from Marissa's list is met; declare P1 and notify both teams
- Diagnostic artifacts: attaching diag-snapshot-07-25.log (trimmed) — it contains last week's KV churn sample which motivated the medium risk rating.

I'll update the runbook with the explicit no-key-rotation note and the trace artifact template.

— Neha
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepayments.com>, SaaS Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC patch window — risk heatmap & ops check-in

Thanks everyone — alignment notes and concrete next steps below. We should treat this as the agreed runbook unless someone objects by EOD 2028-07-27.

Decisions: 
- Final window: Sat 2028-08-03 03:30-07:30 UTC (per Jordan's request). Canary at 03:45 UTC.
- Canary spike: Redwood will run the 10% load spike during the 30m soak and share traces. Acme to provide sample request profile by 2028-07-27 12:00 UTC.
- KV key rotation: out of scope for this window (explicitly no rotation).
- Rollback & abort triggers: adopt the list Marissa proposed; add one: sustained increase >30% CPU across pinned nodes for 15m.

Operational checklist (owner annotations):
1) Pre-warm initiated 90m prior — owner: Neha (will post run id)
2) Canary deployment job — owner: Karthik (job id and link to succeed)
3) Synthetic spike script ready & test run in staging — owner: Rishi
4) Customer on-call confirmed (Samir) & backup ops@acmepayments.com — owner: Marissa
5) Post-mortem template & incident contact list attached to runbook — owner: Marissa/Acme Sec

Comms plan:
- 24h pre-notice to Acme app teams (Marissa)
- Live Slack bridge in #acme-redwood during window (Karthik will provision)
- Post-window 2-hour war room if any abort occurs (Rishi lead)

Attachments published to the shared folder; I'll add final run IDs and job links once created. If no objections, I'll record this decision in OPS-4123 and send the calendar invite with the bridge.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability & Platform
Redwood Inference
